D2 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — REPAIRED. WAS: the exemption register declared a granularity of role x table x operation and the lint enforced none of it. Rows were matched to a table by NAME alone, so a row scoped as narrowly as the shape allows -- {role: 'app_worker', operation: 'select'} -- bought its table a blanket pass, and the same row suppressed rls_enabled as well as rls_forced, which let one register row excuse a tenant table having no row level security at all.

IS NOW: the lint enforces what the catalog can CORROBORATE, and scripts/db/run.mjs and the register's own _what_the_catalog_can_corroborate say plainly what that is. relforcerowsecurity is a TABLE property -- one value for every role and every operation at once -- so it corroborates exactly one row, role '*' with operation 'all', and only such a row suppresses the unforced-table finding. rolbypassrls and rolsuper are ROLE properties holding for every table at once, so a row naming a role is checked against that role's own attributes and suppresses no table finding; naming a table in it narrows nothing. Two cases pin it: a workspace whose NAME carries the marker produces no region at all, and a chatty epilogue does not become rows of the statement it follows.

Still true, still by convention: a statement containing two statements has both outputs folded into one region, and a statement returning no result set parses to [] indistinguishably from a header with no rows. identity-isolation.test.mjs asserts statically that every mutation case carries RETURNING, which is what makes the second safe.
